source.title: The Unintended Trade-off of AI Alignment:Balancing Hallucination Mitigation and Safety in LLMs
source.authors: Omar Mahmoud; Alex Khalil; Buddhika Laknath Semage; T. G. Karimpanal; Santu Rana

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; minor formatting/OCR artifacts do not prevent reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper defines a refusal direction using a harmful-minus-harmless activation difference, but tests refusal behavior by identifying and patching refusal-related attention heads rather than projecting out the single direction at every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The refusal-head ablation results directly test whether removing identified refusal components affects harmful-request responses. The paper also reports harmful-benchmark results for truthfulness interventions and for steering along a hallucination direction; these are recorded as findings outside the listed claim versions. The SAE fine-tuning benchmark comparisons are not rows because they report the proposed method's performance, not an intervention on the claimed single refusal direction. Setup choices and cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The difference-in-means refusal direction is used only as a tool, to generate harmful completions for the contrastive refusal-head dataset (Sec. 4.2.1). The study never ablates, adds or projects out that direction and reports refusal rates. Its causal test patches out 20 selected attention heads. That is a component-level intervention on a different object, so it does not show whether the single direction mediates refusal. The other ASR results come from a LoRA-learned hallucination direction and from ITI/TruthX truthfulness edits, which are not the refusal direction. The fine-tuning tables evaluate the authors' own method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that truthfulness interventions and benign fine-tuning weaken refusal because refusal and hallucination information overlap in some attention heads. They also argue that aggressive alignment suppresses factual knowledge. They propose SAE-identified refusal features with gradient orthogonalization during fine-tuning to keep safety while preserving utility.
record.recipe_differences: The paper defines a refusal direction by a harmful-minus-harmless mean activation difference, then identifies refusal-related heads through contrastive analysis and patches out the top 20 overlapping heads. It does not apply the original single-direction projection at every layer and position or test adding that direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The magnitude of ASR under the rank-1 hallucination-direction steering varies with the steering coefficient and benchmark (Table 1). The head-patching ASR differs between AdvBench and StrongReject.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching out the top-20 attention heads that overlap between refusal and hallucination raises ASR from 0.8% to 53.9% (AdvBench) and from 0.3% to 49.2% (StrongReject) in LLaMA3-8B-Instruct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in LLaMA3-8B-Instruct depends on a small set of attention heads that also carry hallucination signals; knocking them out weakens refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along the negative LoRA-learned hallucination (truthfulness) direction raises harmful-benchmark ASR at |α|≥3 (AdvBench 27.9 to 74.8; StrongReject 40.9 to 66.5), with negligible change at |α|≤2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Truthfulness-enhancing steering along a rank-1 hallucination direction can reduce refusal at strong coefficients.

fits_no_version.finding: ITI and TruthX improve TruthfulQA but raise AdvBench/StrongReject ASR relative to the base model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Truthfulness interventions trade safety for factuality.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The refusal-head ablation tests a selected set of 20 heads, not the claimed single direction, and does not report a capability check for that ablation. Uncertainty estimates are not stated. The Figure 3 numerical values are not reliably assignable from the supplied text, so they are left as figure only.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted due to the row limit. Fine-tuning method benchmark comparisons are not extracted as claimed-direction results; the study reports them as evaluations of its proposed method and baselines.

untested.parts: Ablating the difference-in-means direction, adding it to induce refusal, and capability effects are all untested. The direction is only used to generate harmful completions.

missing.what: ITI ASR on LLaMA2-Chat 7B/13B/70B (e.g. 7B AdvBench 25.96%, StrongReject 13.74%). Not refusal-direction evidence, but it extends the truthfulness-safety finding to more models.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 tested/limits_scope verdict should be dropped. The head-patching result concerns localization of refusal in attention heads, not the single residual-stream direction. No general-capability check was run for the head patching. No uncertainty estimates are given. Judge is LlamaGuard3.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not directly project out the difference-in-means refusal direction at every layer and position, add that direction to induce refusal on harmless requests, or report general-capability effects of the refusal-head ablation.

relation.reason: The direction is applied operationally as a tool, defined as the mean activation difference between harmful and harmless prompts, and its effect is never measured.

tranche.reason: The difference-in-means refusal direction is used only to generate harmful completions for the refusal-head dataset (Sec. 4.2.1). No refusal rate is reported for ablating, adding or projecting out that direction. The causal tests are head patching and steering along a rank-1 hallucination direction. These are different constructs that fit no version.

source_check.notes: The venue (EACL) is not stated in the text, which shows only the arXiv v2 header. On the refusal-head data source, Appendix B.2 (157 StrongReject prompts jailbroken by the LoRA direction) differs from Sec. 4.2.1 (completions from the refusal direction). Appendix Table 5 gives ITI ASR on LLaMA2-Chat 7B/13B/70B with no rows; these fit no version.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Top-20 refusal/hallucination-head patching on AdvBench and StrongReject
reader_labels.reason: Patching these heads sharply raises ASR, but the reported rates remain below complete compliance and the intervention is not the all-layer, all-position single-direction ablation; see R1–R2.
